newsitem.title: NORWAY: Kvaerner says readying Australia project.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner says readying Australia project.

text.p: Kvaerner ASA, the London-based international engineering and construction group, said on Thursday it had made progress in a move to take control of the next stage of development of the US$1.5 billion AUSI iron project in Western Australia.

At an Extraordinary General Meeting of AUSI this week, shareholders approved of Kvaerner's key development role in the project, although a number of conditions have yet to be determined, Kvaerner said in a statement.
All existing shareholders will retain their rights to participate to the same degree in the project, it said.
The AUSI iron project will produce 4 mtpa of DRI pellets using high-grade Western Australian iron ore fines and natural gases for sale into Asia, including significant contracts into China.

"Kvaerner has already invested more than US$7 million in the AUSI project and will be continuing with the development of the project while seeking the participation of other major investors," John Fletcher, chairman of Kvaerner Corporate Development, said.
